questions.q: Which Excel function is used to count the number of cells that contain numbers?
questions.x: 'COUNT' function specifically counts only numeric values in a range.

questions.q: What does the 'Paste Special' option in Excel allow you to do?
o: Only copy formatting from one cell to another
Copy values, formulas, or formatting selectively
questions.x: 'Paste Special' lets you choose between values, formulas, formatting, or other specific data types.

questions.q: Which shortcut key is used to create a new worksheet in Excel?
questions.x: Shift + F11 inserts a new worksheet in the current workbook.

questions.q: What does the 'VLOOKUP' function in Excel do?
o: Looks up values vertically in a table
Looks up values horizontally in a table
Calculates the sum of a range
questions.x: 'VLOOKUP' searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value in the same row from a specified column.

questions.q: Which Excel feature allows you to apply predefined formats to cells?
questions.x: 'Cell Styles' provide a quick way to apply consistent formatting like fonts, colors, and borders.

questions.q: Which protocol is used for sending emails over the internet?
questions.x: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the standard protocol for email transmission.

questions.q: What does the acronym 'ISP' stand for in networking?
questions.x: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider, which offers internet access to users.

questions.q: Which of these is a wired internet connection type?
questions.x: Ethernet uses cables (like RJ-45) for wired internet connectivity.
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of data communication on the web.

questions.q: Which of these is a public IP address?
questions.x: Public IPs (like 203.123.45.67) are globally routable, unlike private ranges (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x).

questions.q: What is the full form of 'URL'?
questions.x: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a web resource.

questions.q: Which of these is a peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing protocol?
questions.x: BitTorrent is a P2P protocol used for distributing large files among users.
A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates a secure, encrypted tunnel for data transmission.
